project.name: AI-Based Recruitment and Resume Screening System
project.description: An AI system that parses resumes, extracts skills and experience, and automatically scores and ranks candidates for open job roles. Recruiters receive a ranked shortlist, and candidates scoring below a threshold are automatically rejected before any human reads their application. The company receives thousands of applications per role.
project.data_used: Resumes, cover letters, past hiring decisions and performance ratings, application forms with name, gender, age, address and education
project.users: Recruiters and hiring managers as users; job applicants as affected people
project.deployment: Cloud SaaS integrated with the company's applicant tracking system; runs on every incoming application

risks.title: Hiring objectives and fairness criteria undefined
risks.description: The company has not defined what a fair shortlist means, so success is measured only as speed, and discrimination risks are never assessed.
risks.mitigation: Define fairness objectives and acceptable-risk thresholds up front; involve HR, legal and employee representatives.

risks.title: Violation of employment and anti-discrimination law
risks.description: Automated screening may breach equal-opportunity laws and rules on automated employment decision tools, including bias audit and notice requirements.
risks.mitigation: Legal review per jurisdiction; run a bias audit before launch; provide candidate notices; maintain compliance documentation.

risks.title: Historical hiring data encodes demographic bias
risks.description: Training on past hiring decisions teaches the model to repeat earlier preferences for certain genders, colleges or age groups.
risks.mitigation: Audit historical outcomes by group; rebalance or re-label data; avoid using past decisions as the only ground truth.

risks.title: Collecting more personal data than needed
risks.description: Collecting photos, date of birth, marital status and address without purpose creates privacy violations and discrimination risk.
risks.mitigation: Apply data minimisation; drop unnecessary fields at intake; obtain explicit candidate consent and state purpose.

risks.title: Resume parsing errors for non-standard formats
risks.description: Parsers mis-read multi-column layouts, non-English resumes or career gaps, so qualified candidates appear to lack skills.
risks.mitigation: Test parsers on diverse formats and languages; add human review for parse failures; track parse-quality metrics.

risks.title: Proxy features that reveal protected attributes
risks.description: Name, postcode, university or hobbies can act as proxies for gender, caste, religion or ethnicity and silently drive the ranking.
risks.mitigation: Anonymise names and photos; run proxy analysis; remove or constrain correlated features.

risks.title: Unfair candidate ranking from a biased model
risks.description: The ranking model gives systematically lower scores to women, older applicants or candidates from less-known institutions with equal qualifications.
risks.mitigation: Apply fairness-aware training or post-processing; set parity constraints; compare against a transparent baseline model.

risks.title: Opaque scoring that cannot be explained to candidates
risks.description: Neither recruiters nor candidates can see why a score was given, which blocks challenge and breaks transparency obligations.
risks.mitigation: Use interpretable features or SHAP explanations; produce a per-candidate reason summary; publish a model card.

risks.title: Incorrect rejection of qualified candidates
risks.description: False negatives automatically reject strong candidates before any human sees them, harming individuals and the company's talent pool.
risks.mitigation: Measure false-rejection rate; audit a random sample of rejected applications; lower thresholds and route borderline cases to humans.

risks.title: No bias audit using subgroup metrics
risks.description: Overall accuracy is reported but selection-rate ratios across demographic groups are never tested, hiding adverse impact.
risks.mitigation: Compute selection-rate ratios and equal-opportunity gaps; use an independent auditor; document the results.

risks.title: Security breach exposing applicant data
risks.description: Resume databases hold sensitive personal data and are attractive targets; prompt or file injection in resumes could also manipulate scores.
risks.mitigation: Encryption, access control and logging; sanitise uploaded files; test for adversarial resume content; vendor security review.

risks.title: No human oversight of automated rejections
risks.description: Candidates are rejected without a recruiter reviewing the decision and without any appeal route, removing accountability.
risks.mitigation: Require human review of all rejections or at least borderline ones; provide an appeal channel; record who made the final decision.

risks.title: Candidates gaming the system with keyword stuffing
risks.description: Applicants learn which keywords the model rewards and add hidden text, which degrades ranking validity and disadvantages honest candidates.
risks.mitigation: Detect hidden text and keyword stuffing; refresh features regularly; monitor score distributions for sudden shifts.

risks.title: Fairness drift as the applicant pool changes
risks.description: Changing job markets and applicant demographics shift the data so that a model that was fair at launch becomes biased later.
risks.mitigation: Monthly fairness dashboard; automatic alert on selection-rate gaps; retrain with refreshed data.

risks.title: Applicant data kept indefinitely after retirement
risks.description: Rejected candidates' resumes and model logs stay in storage after the tool is switched off, breaching retention limits.
risks.mitigation: Apply a retention schedule; delete or anonymise applicant data; confirm deletion with the vendor in writing.

risks.title: Loss of decision records for later disputes
risks.description: Decommissioning the screening tool without archiving decisions and explanations makes it impossible to answer later discrimination complaints.
risks.mitigation: Archive decision logs and explanations for the legal retention period; document the model version and thresholds.
